value: Greater activation of the rostral PFC was associated with greater activation of several brain regions in quitting-unmotivated smokers anticipating an opportunity to smoke, including the superior frontal gyrus, anterior/dorsal and posterior cingulate gyri, dorsal and ventral striatum, and medial PFC extending to the rostral ACC and OFC. Quitting-motivated smokers showed a different pattern, including a non-significant negative relationship between rostral PFC and medial PFC/rostral ACC/OFC activation. These findings indicate that quitting motivation modulated functional connectivity during cigarette cue exposure.
